title: staged-kv-index-drift-oom-guard-and-runtime-fix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Several Private and Dedicated customer clusters have experienced delayed GPU OOM cascades over multi-hour windows. Root cause analysis points to a deterministic but slow drift in the KV index mapping across async compaction + allocator prefetch logic, which created shadow entries and prevented timely eviction. The effect: per-session tensor arenas grew unbounded for certain long-running chat sessions and batch patterns, eventually saturating GPUs and triggering OOMs. Scope: observed 3 enterprise customers on Private (EU, us-west) and 1 Dedicated cluster; hosted instances showed transient pressure but no full OOMs. This ticket tracks the runtime patch, validation, and rollout plan to add a preemptive OOM-guard + index-resync, along with telemetry and postmortem actions.
reproduction_steps: Start a long-lived chat session and stream multiple large-context messages with repeated prefix access (simulate conversational agent with 8-12k prompt).
Run continuous batched requests at bursty QPS that exercise KV prefetch and allocator prewarm paths.
Allow async compaction to run while repeated session handles are used across worker handoff to emulate multi-tenant tenant-shuffle.
Observe gradual growth in arena usage on the serving node via tensor_pool and GPU memory dashboard until OOM occurs (~3-6 hours in our test harness).
mitigation: Deployed emergency config to Private clusters: aggressive KV tombstone sweep and reduced allocator prefetch window (config: allocator.prefetch_ms=50).
Added temporary per-session tensor_pool cap to limit unbounded growth (config: runtime.session_tensor_cap=2GB) — reduces customer throughput but prevents OOM cascade.
Activated regional fallback policies for impacted customers to route new requests to alternate Dedicated capacity while fix is validated.
Opened high-priority support channels with affected customers and provided runbooks and temporary quotas.
resolution_plan: 1) Introduce runtime preemptive OOM-guard that detects growing mismatch between KV index metadata and live handle set; when threshold exceeded, trigger synchronous index-resync and compact hot tombstones.
2) Fix allocator-prefetch race: ensure prefetch only marks slots after successful slab reservation (see PR #428-prereflect).
3) Add a lightweight periodic KV index checksum and repair agent that runs low-priority compaction when drift > 0.5%.
4) Unit + integration tests: extend existing multi-tenant stress tests to include tenant handoff and compaction races for 48-hour windows. Add GPU memory assertions to CI harness.
5) Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across Private clusters with health metrics gating and automatic rollback on increased OOM rate.
6) Postmortem and runbook: document detector thresholds, ops playbook, and include a Simulation checklist for customer migrations.
